stemMd: Which statement must be true in every permitted order?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Memory must not be in position 1.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Cities must not be in position 1.

explanationMd:
Combine the ordering and placement constraints rather than assuming one example is unique. The statement "Memory must not be in position 1." holds in all 4 permitted orders. Generate the cases by placing any fixed-position item and adjacent block first, then discard arrangements that violate a remaining rule. For each alternative, an explicit permitted counterexample appears in its feedback.

Complete permitted orders (each arrow advances one position):
- Cities → Memory → Customs → Work → Letters
- Cities → Memory → Letters → Work → Customs
- Customs → Memory → Letters → Cities → Work
- Letters → Memory → Customs → Cities → Work

distractorRationale.c: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Cities → Memory → Customs → Work → Letters. Thus this statement is not necessary.
distractorRationale.b: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Cities → Memory → Customs → Work → Letters. Thus this statement is not necessary.
distractorRationale.d: A counterexample satisfying all the rules is Customs → Memory → Letters → Cities → Work. Thus this statement is not necessary.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Blind re-solve in the 5 November 2026 AI audit of this expansion (the review packet held no key, explanation or distractor notes; status "verified_key_agreement"; it checked for competing defensible answers and flagged none): Independently enumerated all 120 permutations of Cities, Customs, Letters, Memory, Work. Rules Memory must be in position 2. Cities must precede Work. Exactly 1 other item must occur between Customs and Letters. leave 4 valid orders: Cities>Memory>Customs>Work>Letters; Cities>Memory>Letters>Work>Customs; Customs>Memory>Letters>Cities>Work; Letters>Memory>Customs>Cities>Work. Choice true counts: a=2, b=2, c=4, d=2; necessary requires all matches.
